name: Shackleton Crater · rim (lunar South Pole, Artemis site «Shackleton rim»)

imagery.credit: Hillshade computed from LRO LOLA LDEM_80S_40M (Sun at 315°/35°); not a photograph
imagery.product: 1024 px hillshade at 18.75 m/px from the 40.0 m DEM, edges = bbox of the 19200 m window

dataset: LRO LOLA LDEM_80S_40M (polar stereographic GDR, 40 m/px, v2.1 2017; NASA GSFC / PDS Geosciences)

centerBias.definition: context − scenario (m), mean of the central 2.4 km

sampling.frame: local azimuthal equidistant centered on `center` (row 0 = north, column 0 = west) · sphere R = 1737400 m
sampling.node: area average of the 200 m cell centered on the node
sampling.elevationDatum: height (km × 1000 → m) relative to the 1737.4 km sphere

provenance.label: LRO LOLA LDEM_80S_40M (polar stereographic GDR, 40 m/px, v2.1 2017; NASA GSFC / PDS Geosciences)

notes: The PGDA LOLA 5 m Site04 LDEM (16 × 16 km) covers only 65% of the nodes of the 19.2 km window; for the context LRO LOLA LDEM_80S_40M (polar stereographic GDR, 40 m/px, v2.1 2017; NASA GSFC / PDS Geosciences) is used, without mixing it with the DTM of the measured window (avoids artificial seams). The level difference between both products is kept in centerBiasM.

Each node is the area average of the product at ~200 m (HTTP range reads of the needed rows and block averaging) sampled bilinearly in the local azimuthal equidistant frame of the 1737400 m sphere (row 0 = north, column 0 = west), same as the measured window.
The 19.2 km window includes the south pole (~6.6 km from the center): the LDEM polar stereographic projection has no singularity there.
The image is a hillshade computed from the context DEM itself (Sun at 315°/35°, like the measured window), not a photograph: at the Shackleton rim illumination is almost always grazing or absent.
centerBiasM = -19.2 m: mean of the 13×13 central context nodes (2.4 km) = 1511.0 m versus the scenario grid mean = 1530.2 m. The frontend subtracts this bias so the context joins the measured window.
Lower-resolution context to fill the horizon around the measured 2400 m window; it is not measured data of that window and does not enter metrics or comparisons (metrics = null).
